articles.title: Meta planerar nyemission på närmare 1 biljon
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Meta planerar nyemission på närmare 1 biljon
articles.body_text: Metas vd Mark Zuckerberg vill ha mer pengar. Arkivbild. Meta planerar nyemission på närmare 1 biljon Meta behöver ett jättetillskott av pengar och ber ägarna om 95 miljarder dollar för att investera i AI. Meta, bolaget bakom Facebook och Instagram, lanserade på måndagen en plan för att dra in motsvarande 940 miljarder kronor. Tillskottet ska ske via en nyemission av aktier där pengarna ska gå till AI-investeringar de kommande åren, skriver Financial Times. Nvidia, AMD och Broadcom har lovat att ställa upp som ankarinvesterare.

articles.title: AI hämtade väljardata utan mänskligt godkännande
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: AI hämtade väljardata utan mänskligt godkännande
articles.body_text: Anthropic ingår ett mångmiljardavtal. Arkivbild. AI hämtade väljardata utan mänskligt godkännande Ännu en incident har upptäckts där en AI agerar på eget bevåg. Anthropics AI-modell Claude har hämtat data om väljare i Georgia, rapporterar Axios. Enligt en talesperson för Anthropic hämtade modellen, som tränades inom ramen för ett internt statistikprojekt, information bakom en betalvägg genom att kringgå systemet ”utan att ha blivit ombedd att göra det”. Modellen kom inte åt delstatens system för väljarregistrering och ändrade eller hämtade inte några röstningsuppgifter, enligt talespersonen, men händelsen är den senaste i raden av säkerhetsincidenter hos världens ledande AI-utvecklare inför de viktiga amerikanska mellanårsvalen den 3 november. Anthropic ska nu ha vidtagit åtgärder för att förhindra att något liknande sker igen.

articles.title: Extremvärmen tvingar H&M att tänka nytt
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Extremvärmen tvingar H&M att tänka nytt
articles.body_text: Andreas Löwenstam är huvuddesigner för H&M:s herrkollektion. Här på plats vid företagets huvudkontor i Stockholm. Återkommande värmeböljor och extremvärme ställer även modeindustrin inför nya utmaningar. Vilka material eller plagg fungerar och när ska egentligen höst- och vinterkollektioner lanseras? H&M är ett av flera bolag som försöker hitta svaren. I mitten av augusti var Andreas Löwenstam på tjänsteresa i Barcelona. Som design lead för H&M:s herravdelning var han i Spanien för att träffa bolagets leverantörer. Vi kom ned dit och det var typ 40 grader. Det här är kanske den största utmaningen och jag vet inte ens om vi tänkte i de här banorna för fem år sedan – nu måste vi göra det, säger han. Efter att tidigare varit stationerad i Asien för H&M har han stor erfarenhet av höga temperaturer och ett utmanande klimat. Under senare år har detta också blivit en verklighet i Syd- och Mellaneuropa med kraftiga och återkommande värmeböljor. Nyligen rapporterade också den världsmeteorologiska organisationen WMO om hur klimatfenomenet El Niño den här säsongen förväntas bli det mest kraftfulla någonsin. Klimatförändringar är något som påverkar hela klädbranschen där behoven och skillnaderna mellan olika regioner kan bli allt större, påpekar Andreas Löwenstam: Det är ett mindset, man förstår att Indien, Miami eller Indonesien har andra behov, men vi ser absolut att vi behöver tänka om när det gäller vad vi gör för södra respektive norra Europa. H&M-gruppen är en av världens största aktörer inom klädindustrin med drygt 4 000 butiker runt om i världen. Utanför huvudkontoret i centrala Stockholm råder klassiskt höstväder, snålblåst och regn. Inne i lokalen arbetar Andreas Löwenstam och hans kollegor med vad kunderna kan tänkas vilja ha på sig en sommardag 2027. Rent företagsekonomiskt handlar det om att kunna ta beslut när olika kollektioner ska plockas bort och nya lanseras. Till sin hjälp har H&M väderdata och analyser som sträcker sig flera decennier tillbaka i tiden, berättar vd:n Daniel Ervér: När sker skiftet till höst? När ska vi börja visa stickat? articles.title: Oväntat positiv stämning bland tyska företag
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Oväntat positiv stämning bland tyska företag
articles.body_text: En månatlig mätning av stämningen bland tyska företag från Ifo-institutet i München visar på återhämtning. Arkivbild Oväntat positiv stämning bland tyska företag Stämningsläget bland tyska företag blir oväntat bättre för sjätte månaden i rad i oktober, enligt en indikator från Ifo-institutet i München. ”Den ekonomiska återhämtningen fortsätter”, skriver Ifo-chefen Clemens Fuest i ett pressmeddelande. Ifo-index för oktober steg till 91,6, upp från 90,4 i september. Snittprognosen bland analytiker låg på en mindre nedgång för indexet, till 90,0, i oktober. Ett delindex för synen på nuläget försämrades samtidigt något, vilket inte heller det var väntat. Tyska regeringen höjde nyligen sin tillväxtprognos för 2026 till 1,3 procent – trots inflationsproblem och värmeböljor som slagit hårt mot transportsystemet. Den tyska ekonomin växer till stor del tack vare stora investeringar i infrastruktur, försvar och AI.

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Ebola outbreak: Uganda imposes 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from DR Congo
articles.summary: Uganda will also not allow most travellers who have been in DR Congo to transit through the country.
articles.body_text: Ugandans returning from neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, the health ministry has said, as the country tightens restrictions to contain the spread of Ebola virus. More than 4,800 people have died in DR Congo since May - the country's deadliest outbreak of the disease - and has since spread to several other countries. Uganda's restrictions follow questions after two people who had travelled through the country tested positive for Ebola, in Kenya and Nigeria. The health ministry on Sunday said the 60 people who were being monitored after coming into contact with the Kenyan Ebola patient had all been discharged. Announcing the new measures on Sunday, the health ministry said travellers who had been to DR Congo would not be allowed to transit through Uganda. It said returning Ugandans would "undergo 21 days of quarantine at their own cost". Uganda has also "intensified traveller screening at Entebbe International Airport and all land border crossings, supported by screening at designated road checkpoints", it added. Uganda's Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi told the BBC's Newsday programme that only essential travellers from DR Congo would be allowed in but would be subjected to "intense public health measures". "All these are measures to ensure that we keep Uganda free of Ebola," he said. Since the two cases were reported in Kenya and Nigeria this month, Uganda has repeatedly stressed that no cases have been reported within its borders. Uganda recorded 20 Ebola cases and two people died shortly after the outbreak started in DR Congo, but the World Health Organization declared the country free of the disease in August. Concerns have however persisted after the two passengers tested positive after passing through Uganda's Entebbe airport on the same day. The patient in Nigeria is the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat who had travelled to the Ugandan capital for a holiday, according to the head of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Jean Kaseya, while the Kenyan had travelled from the DR Congo where he had business interests.

articles.title: Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies aged 46
articles.summary: Bauza had voiced a number of characters in this summer's animated hit Coyote vs. Acme.
articles.body_text: Eric Bauza, the voice artist behind Looney Tunes characters including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died aged 46. A statement from the Emmy award-winning star's family posted on Instagram said he had died "suddenly". Bauza had voiced a number of characters in this summer's animated hit Coyote vs. Acme, and appeared in the recent release Forgotten Island. Variety reports that the cause of death was hypertensive cardiovascular disease and that Bauza died at home on Sunday. In a 2021 interview with NBC News, Bauza, who was born in Ontario and was of Filipino descent, said he grew up a huge fan of the Looney Tunes characters and used to copy the voices as a child. "Looney Tunes transcends all languages and all cultures," he said . "It doesn't matter what part of the planet you're from. You get the comedy." He voiced Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Elmer Fudd and Foghorn Leghorn in 2021's Space Jam: A New Legacy before reprising those roles and that of Road Runner in Coyote vs. Acme. He also played the part of Toad General in 2023's The Super Mario Bros. Movie and its sequel The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, the fifth highest-grossing film internationally this year. Between 2022 and 2025, he won three Emmy awards for outstanding voice performance in a number of TV series. In a statement reported by the Hollywood Reporter , Channing Dungey, the chairman of Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks, said: "Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world. "He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc. Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life."

articles.title: Australian murderer loses bid to eat Vegemite in prison
articles.summary: Andre McKechnie, who murdered a property developer, argued it was his right to enjoy Australian culture.
articles.body_text: A convicted murderer serving a life sentence in Australia has lost his bid to overturn a ban on prisoners consuming Vegemite - the salty yeast-based spread that has become a national symbol. Andre McKechnie argued that the ban, in place since 2006, denied him the right to "enjoy his culture as an Australian". Authorities in the state of Victoria say inmates may use the strong-smelling paste to disguise contraband substances or to brew alcohol behind bars. And on Monday, a Supreme Court judge rejected McKechnie's appeal, saying the prisoner's "cultural rights are limited primarily by the fact he has been sentenced to a term of imprisonment". In his lawsuit against Victoria's Department of Justice and Corrections, the agency which manages the state's prisons, McKechnie, 54, said the ban on the spread breached law requiring prisons to provide food that allowed inmates to maintain their health and well-being but the judge said that had not been proven. McKechnie was handed a life sentence for stabbing a property developer to death in Queensland in the 1990s. He served part of his sentence in Queensland before being transferred to Victoria. During the hearing, the court heard evidence from Corrections Victoria that the smell of vegemite can distract sniffer dogs trying to detect drugs being brought into prison. The product is also banned in jails in Queensland, South Australia and Tasmania. A much-loved breakfast spread for some, Vegemite has acquired controversial accolades since it first hit shop shelves in Australia in 1923. The thick, brown spread was invented in the Victorian capital of Melbourne more than a century ago as an alternative to the British spread Marmite. It sparked an international dispute in April last year when an Australian cafe owner in Canada was told to remove jars of the condiment from his shelves as it did not comply with local health regulations. Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese intervened in the row, saying it was "rather odd" that Canada allowed the sale of Vegemite's "rubbish" rival product Marmite. The cafe owner was later allowed to continue selling the spread.

articles.title: Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
articles.summary: The Super Bass singer is the latest big name to campaign in Michigan, where a tight Senate race is playing out ahead of the 3 November midterms.
articles.body_text: Rapper Nicki Minaj said US President Donald Trump has "changed the energy of the country" as she joined him at a Michigan rally to stump for Republicans ahead of the nationwide midterm elections. "He's given us a future to look forward to," she said, after Trump praised her figure and called her on stage to speak. Minaj has called herself Trump's "number one fan" despite criticising some of his policies in his first term. In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is locked in a tight race with Republican Mike Rogers with just over a week to go before the midterms. Former President Barack Obama held a rally - one of the first in this cycle - with the Democrat on Saturday. Democrats are also aggressively hitting the campaign trail, with close elections taking place on 3 November which will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's presidency. In his remarks on Sunday, Trump focused on El-Sayed's Muslim faith and background, alleging that he will "invite jihadists" into America if he wins. El-Sayed has criticised similar remarks by Trump as Islamophobic, saying in an ad to voters last week that the US president "thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor's office". In Port Huron on Sunday, Minaj, wearing a gold-coloured Gucci-branded suit, led the crowd in chanting Trump's name, and the names of Republican candidates in Michigan. "We really need all these great people to be elected, because this is a major turning point for our country," she said. "She never looked more beautiful," Trump said as she left the stage. "She gets it. She's smart," he added. Earlier in his speech, Trump praised the rear end of one male Republican candidate before turning the crowd's attention to Minaj. "By the way, I looked at a beautiful ass before," he segued. "Nicki Minaj. That's hard to miss."

articles.title: Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election
articles.summary: After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming, writes Lucy Williamson.
articles.body_text: After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming. The general election on Tuesday hangs over a country that's deeply divided and ready for a fight. Polls published on Friday put the governing coalition and the main opposition bloc almost neck-and-neck, with half a million first-time voters due to cast their ballot and some 70,000 Israelis reportedly flying in from abroad specifically to vote. On Saturday night, vast crowds of opposition voters gathered in central Tel Aviv to demand a change of government. "We're optimistic," 21-year-old Omri told me. "I want peace, I want security, and I want to end corruption and get the religious fanatics out." This campaign has been energized by new tactics - including AI videos designed to grab the headlines - and also by a new face. Gadi Eisenkot is, perhaps, not the man you might expect to take on the flashy, aggressive, media-savvy brand of Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. Relatively new to politics, with a working-class Moroccan background, Eisenkot is a former military chief of staff who is renowned for his calm manner and low-drama approach. He's been dubbed by some as a "non-politician". But he and his centrist Yashar party have regularly pipped Netanyahu and his Likud party to the top spot in recent polls, the last of which was published on Friday, in line with Israeli election law. Israeli politics is the art of coalition-building, rather than the task of any one party winning power, but with the predicted result too close to call, Eisenkot's rising profile has sharpened a race many Israelis already see as existential for the future of their country. I watched him slip past the cameras at a community centre for Ethiopian Jews in the city of Ramle last week, through a gaggle of security personnel and advisors. One of those who had come to hear him speak was David, a smartly dressed man in a freshly-pressed shirt and navy jacket, who said he had met Eisenkot before.

articles.title: Serbia's veteran ruler Vučić concedes election to student-led protest movement
articles.summary: The populist right-wing leader of 12 years says it is "clear" his party has lost the vote billed as a referendum on the country's future.
articles.body_text: Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to a student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. Celebrations erupted as crowds descended on the centre of Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities. The student movement was formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption and negligence, but fought the election with candidates from a cross-section of Serbian society. "It is clear we have lost these elections," right-wing populist leader Vučić said as he conceded. With 96% of polling stations counted, Serbia's election commission said the students had won 2.24 million votes and the former ruling party 1.67 million. The students had secured 52.65% of the vote, while Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) was on 39.2%, according to its preliminary figures late on Monday morning. Vučić had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017. He called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a canopy in front of Novi Sad station which killed 16 people. The Student List's lead candidate Ilija Srdanović told BBC Serbian: "This will be a free state." He said the anti-corruption movement, which had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia, hoped to "free the country from tyranny". There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle." During a celebration speech, Student List candidate Radomir Saicic said Serbians had shown "no obstacle was greater than their will", Reuters reported. "No force can forever overpower a people who have decided to take their destiny into their own hands," he added. Amid scenes of people dancing in the streets Belgrade, Selena Lebovic said the result was "really fabulous".

articles.title: Opposition leader María Machado returns to Venezuela
articles.summary: Machado had left the country just a month before the US government seized Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.
articles.body_text: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile. "I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail. In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US. Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands. She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters have lined the route of her journey to the capital. She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of the sunroof of a car as she entered Caracas late on Sunday night. "Night of reunion in our Caracas. For the reunion of each family, for the Freedom of each political prisoner, for the Freedom of Venezuela," she wrote on X. Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: "I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil." "Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" González said. He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country "toward freedom". An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. articles.title: Suspect in deadly Paris suburb shooting sent for psychiatric observation
articles.summary: He will be observed to evaluate whether his "psychiatric health is compatible with pursuing his interrogation", authorities said.
articles.body_text: A man suspected of a deadly gun attack near Paris has left custody and been placed under psychiatric observation, French anti-terrorism officials have said. One person was killed and five others injured on Friday when an attacker opened fire from his car - first in Trappes, and then in nearby La Verrière - appearing to target people of migrant origin. The suspect, named in French media as 39-year-old Kevin T, will be observed to evaluate whether his "psychiatric health is compatible with pursuing his interrogation", the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) said. President Emmanuel Macron called it a "racist terrorist attack", adding that people had been targeted over their skin colour or religion. It marked a "turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation", the French president said. PNAT said the move to place the suspect under psychiatric evaluation followed guidance from a psychiatric expert. The evaluation will determine whether the suspect should remain in police custody and is "likely to last 48 hours", PNAT added. PNAT said the suspect was also found to have cannabis and cocaine in his bloodstream. French newspaper Le Monde and news agency AFP report that a Bible, a Quran and a copy of Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf were found at the suspect's home, citing a source close to the investigation. The lawyer for Pengo Bossio Wangi, the one person killed during the attack, told French media the move to place the suspect under observation was "very rare". He alleged that it was being used to portray the suspect as criminally irresponsible rather than having acted deliberately. Wangi, a 26-year-old French-Congolese martial artist, was named as the one fatality on Saturday.

articles.title: Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection as service restored
articles.summary: The tech billionaire accuses Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using the network for military activity.
articles.body_text: Elon Musk has said his company SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service, after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved. The tech billionaire accused Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using it for military activity - but denied being responsible for a simultaneous issue with its US-run, military-grade counterpart Starshield. Kyiv has not officially commented on Musk's latest claim but Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said his post was "very strange". Musk had earlier denied deliberately throttling Ukraine's connection, which it says hampered its ability to conduct defensive operations for more than a week. The issue first emerged last week during a broader row between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Musk's latest comments, and the seeming restoration of the service, came after US President Donald Trump said he had told the Tesla and X owner to "put it back", having repeatedly denied instructing him to limit the service. "Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote on X on Saturday. "Ukraine['s] military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week." He went on to say that SpaceX had "done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth" and reiterated his stipulation that Starshield was a different system and controlled by the US government, adding: "What they decide to do is up to them." He added in a later post: "[Starlink] can be used for infrastructure that is military, but it cannot be used for unequivocally offensive strikes that make it fair game to be struck back." Reacting to Musk's post, Beskrestnov said that drones operating via Starlink in Ukraine had a speed restriction of 70-90km/h (43-56mph) and did not work on Russian territory. "Therefore, we physically cannot use commercial Starlink for deep strikes and medium-range strikes," he wrote on Telegram.

articles.title: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates
articles.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announces restrictions on the movement of Palestinian workers in the run-up to Tuesday's election.
articles.body_text: All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements. The restrictions come amid a crackdown in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the territory. The Israel Defense Forces announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday. It said most workers would also be barred from settlements from Sunday, with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas. Before the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel. Since then only a small fraction have had their permits restored. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major operation on Friday in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed. The Israeli military have been demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron, with hundreds of families having been displaced . Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation, which has led to at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened, according to footage shared online. Even before the entry and exit bans on workers were announced by the IDF on Sunday, the military had cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents. It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis in the West Bank - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment. Friday's shooting came during a tense time for the region, just days ahead of Israel's election taking place on Tuesday. In an interview with Israel's i24 television channel released on Saturday, Netanyahu threatened a "very big surprise" for the Palestinian Authority (PA), which governs parts of the territory.

articles.title: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.summary: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. En el caso de los servidores públicos, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días inmediatos posteriores o en la oportunidad que establezca el titular de cada entidad, según sus necesidades. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. articles.summary: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. En el caso de los servidores públicos, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días inmediatos posteriores o en la oportunidad que establezca el titular de cada entidad, según sus necesidades. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: The best apps for tracking your reading and discovering new books | TechCrunch
articles.summary: There are many apps that are designed to help you track your reading and discover new books, so we compiled a list of some of the best ones.
articles.body_text: From discovering new books and organizing your reading list to tracking your reading goal and sharing recommendations, book apps make it easier to maintain reading as a hobby. There are numerous apps on the market that promise to do just that, so we’ve compiled a list of some of the best ones to help you pick the right one for you. Whether you’re an occasional reader or a dedicated bookworm, these apps can help you make the most of your reading journey. Some of the apps on this list are somewhat new, while others have been around for a few years. Amazon-owned Goodreads, which is arguably the most popular book-related app, isn’t included in this list because we’re focusing on newer, lesser-known platforms. Fable is a reading app that combines book tracking with a social platform. It lets you organize reading lists, set reading goals, track streaks, write reviews, and join virtual book clubs. You also get personalized book recommendations and the chance to discuss what you’re reading with other readers. The app differs from others on this list because it puts reading and community at the forefront of the platform, which makes it a great option for people who like staying motivated to read by being part of a community and discussing their reads. Fable is free to download on iOS and Android , but also offers a Fable Plus subscription tier that unlocks additional features like custom goals and advanced analytics for a monthly fee of $5.99. Bookshelf is a reading app designed to help people organize their libraries, discover new books, and remember more of what they read. The app positions itself as an alternative to Goodreads, and combines traditional reading logs with AI-powered recommendations and tools. You can create custom shelves, set reading goals, receive reminders, save favorite quotes, and access AI-generated book summaries, key insights, and thematic analyses to recall the books you’ve read and get a deeper understanding of them. Bookshelf is free to download on iOS , but offers a $6.99 monthly fee to unlock premium features like unlimited collections and enhanced analytics. Pagebound is a book app that lets readers track their books, create lists, set goals, and discuss individual titles in dedicated forums. Instead of having to join an actual book club group, users can post reactions and thoughts to connect with others reading the same title. You don’t have to worry about spoilers for the end of the book, as conversations are organized based on reading progress, allowing readers to share theories and thoughts as they read. The app is a great option for people who want to discuss their reads with others without having to commit to a scheduled book club. Pagebound is free to download on iOS and Android and offers a $9.99 monthly subscription for added features like profile customization. StoryGraph is a reading app that lets users track their reading, discover new books, and access detailed reading statistics and personalized recommendations. Users can set reading goals, join reading challenges, and find new titles based on their preferred moods, themes, genres, and pacing.

articles.title: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated ‘Odyssey’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The footage looks okay, as long as you're not seeking artistry, inspiration, or human interest.
articles.body_text: Three months after Elon Musk declared that Grok would release a full-length, “historically accurate” movie version of “The Odyssey,” Grok has published a whole seven minutes, which the company is now calling “Episode 1 of our Odyssey series.” Musk had previously lashed out at Christopher Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” because Nolan cast nonwhite and transgender actors. And Nolan is, in many ways, a perfect foil for Musk — while SpaceX and Tesla CEO hypes up data centers in space and posts an unending stream of AI-generated content, Nolan has described himself as “a techno-skeptic ” and said that before AI, he’d never seen a technology “so completely rejected by the public.” And while Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” certainly used plenty of visual effects, it’s primarily a feat of practical filmmaking , with a shoot spanning six countries and a cast and crew of thousands. After its release in July, the film became an extraordinary box office success , selling out Imax screenings for months and becoming the likely front-runner at the next Academy Awards . As for the Grok version of “The Odyssey” (created in collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker), well, you can watch for yourself. Watch Episode 1 of our Odyssey series made with Grok Imagine. Let us know in the comments if you'd like a full breakdown of how it was done! Creative collaboration with @WonderStudiosX and director Dev Walker @glumlot_ pic.twitter.com/xpgpkqSCpq I’ll admit it’s not as spectacularly ugly as I’d expected, and certainly more impressive than other videos that Musk has posted recently. If I didn’t know better, there were moments when I might have thought these were real actors sailing across a real sea. And while I can’t speak to Grok’s historical accuracy, it does seem that some fudging was necessary, since no one’s speaking in ancient Greek. But hey, all the characters come in a Musk-approved skin color, while the narrator uses a British accent that will sound familiar to anyone who’s played a fantasy video game or watched a generic Hollywood epic from the past 25 years. What the footage really lacks is any sense of artistry, inspiration, or human interest. The backstory — delivered via the aforementioned voiceover — seems to go on forever, finally giving way to one bearded face after another, each shouting stilted lines that make Nolan’s questionable dialogue (“Our age of bronze is collapsing!”) sound like Shakespeare. While a few individual shots might provide a reasonable simulacrum of reality, as a whole, the clip feels completely airless, offering viewers no sense of momentum, no reason to care about anyone or anything on-screen. And where I had no trouble paying attention for the nearly three hours of Nolan’s “Odyssey,” I was listlessly checking how much time I had left before the Grok version was even halfway through. If it was a video game cutscene, I would have hit the “skip” button. It’s hard to imagine being interested in another seven minutes of this, much less a full movie’s worth. articles.title: ‘Cyberselfish’ author takes aim at techno-libertarianism as her book returns from the dead | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "That's a 12-year-old view of the world."
articles.body_text: It’s hard for books about technology to age well. They always risk becoming outdated as companies rise and fall, and as one hot new product is replaced by the next. But last year, “Nerd Reich” author Gil Durán declared that it was time to revive the career of Paulina Borsook, who he said “saw it all very clearly and tried to warn us 25 years ago.” Later that fall, The New York Times reported that Borsook’s “Cyberselfish ” — first published in 2000 — was finding new fans who want to understand why the tech industry “lost its way.” Now, long after going out of print, “Cyberselfish” is returning in a new edition from Tin House . Borsook told me in a Zoom interview that the book is meant to be “almost a travelogue” of her attempts to understand what she calls the techno-libertarian influence on Silicon Valley culture. “That’s a 12-year-old view of the world,” Borsook said, describing it as “a kind of basket of beliefs” that’s “violently anti-regulation,” despite the fact that “no sector of society had benefited more and suffered less from the government than these guys.” In her telling, “even after the dot-com crash, that attitude was just there, percolating around, contaminating the aquifers. It was uncorrected, and it just spread out more and more.” Borsook has yet to publish a second book, and she said that after “Cyberselfish” was first released, “no one was interested in anything I might have to say about anything, tech or not tech, forever after.” But last year, she began to notice that prices for used copies were beginning to creep up, and she was starting to see “very out-of-the-blue, I-did-not-know-these-people posts on social media about how important this book was,” as well as inquiries from “European academics,” eventually leading to more press coverage and the new Tin House edition, with a new introduction by Durán. Keep reading for our full conversation, edited for length and clarity, in which Borsook discusses AI, how Silicon Valley has transformed in the past 25 years, and what advice she has for young people seeking a career in tech. Do you want to talk a little bit about how your interest in techno-libertarianism started, and how you decided that there was a book in this? Everything with me is always inadvertent. I started knocking around tech circles, however we define it, in the early-middle ‘80s, in the Bay Area. And then I would say, starting around maybe the early ‘90s, I would hear these — to me — very weird, offhand remarks that some people would make that I couldn’t make any sense out of. It’s not my nature to argue with people. It’s my nature to listen, and so I didn’t have the term for it except libertarian. But it seemed very screwy because initially, I grew up in Pasadena, which was [the home of the] Caltech-JPL space program, and so the parents of the kids I knew were another STEM culture. When I first got into Silicon Valley, I thought, “Oh, this is just another STEM culture like I’m familiar with.” And those guys [at Caltech and JPL] had a very clear sense of what the government can do for you, were not into enlightened self-interest. It was a different personality type, and they certainly didn’t self-anoint with how glorious and grand and magisterial they were, even though they were doing great things. I was just listening, I guess, and being confused. Even then, I knew no sector of society had benefited more and suffered less from the government than these guys. So why are they acting like this?

articles.title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech."
articles.body_text: AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch). Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity. “Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said. Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants? Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.” “AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment,” he wrote, later adding, “AI does not understand accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs or fairness, all of which shape reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins.” Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains . articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Blue-green is the color of autonomy | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
articles.body_text: U.S. federal safety regulators continue to tackle the sticky problem of autonomous vehicles, this time with a proposal that could signal to the public, quite literally, when a vehicle is operating autonomously. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has proposed new lighting requirements for autonomous vehicles that include an option (dare I say a strong suggestion?) to use cyan-colored lights to signal when a vehicle is operating autonomously without a human occupant monitoring the road. The agency is not proposing a mandate for blue-green lights. Importantly, under the proposal, the lights would be used when an AV is operating in autonomous mode. Still, federal regulators are clearly seeking some uniform way of identifying autonomous vehicles. The proposal establishes equipment specifications, including where the lights are mounted, the color they emit, and how they’re activated. It would also remove requirements for manually operated controls for turn signals, high beams, and hazard lights. Under the proposal, the NHTSA suggests the lights be cyan (blue-green), remain steadily illuminated rather than flash, and be visible from the front, rear, and both sides. This latest proposal is one piece of a bigger effort to update regulations that help speed up the adoption of AVs while maintaining safety, according to NHTSA administrator Jonathan Morrison. The agency is already working on a federal automated vehicle framework and is trying to update federal motor vehicle safety standards, which already govern automakers today. For instance, FMVSS rules were not designed for vehicles like the Tesla Cybercab and Zoox robotaxi, which lack traditional, federally required equipment like pedals, steering wheels, and design features like side mirrors and rearview mirrors. While the feds wrestle over regulating the future of transportation, GM laid out how it plans to be part of it. The automaker held its annual GM Forward event, and a lot of what was announced builds on last year’s push into AI. But now we have more details and dates. The U.S. automaker is overhauling the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant that will change its 30-year-old OnStar service. This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also roll out an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over. GM has also adopted enterprise AI across the company to slash its traditional four- to five-year development timeline in half.

articles.title: The hottest AI wearables and gadgets you should know about | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We compiled a list of all the hottest AI wearables, including Muse Charm, Bee, Friend, Plaud, and more.
articles.body_text: A slew of AI-powered gadgets on the market aims to integrate artificial intelligence into our daily lives like never before. Some of these AI wearables — including necklaces, rings, and wristbands, as well as portable devices — serve as productivity tools, while others claim to act as friendly companions listening to your everyday thoughts. Even OpenAI is working on a compact AI companion device. Below, we’ve rounded up some of the most notable devices. The companion app (currently available only on iOS) is included with a $19 monthly subscription. The app allows you to interact with Bee directly and ask it questions. You can also get key takeaways from your day and chronological transcripts of your conversations. Amazon acquired the wearables startup in July 2025, launching its first new products earlier this month. Amazon introduced two new devices: the Bee Frontier, priced at $74.99, which can be worn on the wrist or clipped to clothing, and the Bee Eclipse, priced at $99.99, a credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of a smartphone. Both offer the same core functionality as the previous generation, positioning Bee as a more affordable alternative to AI devices such as the Plaud Note and Plaud NotePin. Users can also choose to connect Bee to Alexa. Friend is one of the most hyped entrants in the “personal AI” device market. This $129 white pendant hangs around your neck and functions as an emotional support companion. It recognizes your tone and mood, allowing you to chat with it as if it were a friend. It connects to your phone via Bluetooth and constantly listens, ready to respond or send you proactive messages, like wishing you good luck before an interview. However, it has also faced criticism, including backlash against its subway ad campaign in NYC. People vandalized the ads, writing messages like “surveillance capitalism.” Likely as an attempt to stay relevant, the company recently unveiled a major product update, introducing a new voice feature. Under the name “Friend 2.0,” the updated device includes a built-in speaker that allows it to communicate with users and express a more distinctive personality. Formerly known as Rewind, Limitless is another conversation-recording pendant priced at $99.

articles.title: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Elon Musk reportedly ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine's Starlink access.
articles.body_text: SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions the Ukrainian military’s of use Starshield — the military-grade version of the company’s Starlink internet system. The Wall Street Journal reports that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara told reporters that Starshield appears to be working normally again, although the military is still conducting tests and has not received an explanation for the restrictions. This follows a 10-day period where Ukrainian drones would lose internet connectivity when flying at speeds of around 100 miles per hour, resulting in the military losing control of some drones, while others became more vulnerable because they were flying more slowly. President Donald Trump reportedly called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to restore Starshield service. Both Trump and Musk have criticized Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, with Musk recently posting , “Zelensky has gone too far.” The WSJ previously reported that Musk ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s Starlink access, though some sources claimed he’d discussed it with the Trump administration first. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine had “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people.” “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk said. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.” Buy One Pass, Get a Second Free Cover more ground at TechCrunch’s ultimate founder bootcamp of the year by bringing your co-founder or partner for free Book before the BOGO deal expires Every weekday and Sunday, you can get the best of TechCrunch’s coverage. articles.title: Will AI expose the rickety infrastructure of the internet? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The moment you realize the internet is "held together by glue and dreams."
articles.body_text: A startling announcement went out earlier this week: Due to recently discovered vulnerabilities in the open source programming language PHP, website owners had to immediately patch their sites — or if they couldn’t update right away, they should take the sites down to be safe. On this week’s episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the significance of the PHP-ocalypse and whether we’ll see more incidents like this in the future. Sean called this “a real reckoning moment” that highlights how “when you get down to the bone level of the internet,” everything seems to be “held together by glue and dreams.” And with widespread access to large language models and AI agents, it’s only going to become easier to find these vulnerabilities. (That said, these specific vulnerabilities were found by human researchers , not AI models.) Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity. Sean O’Kane: The internet is breaking in lots of ways this week, it seems. I think the best way to think about this, if people are coming into this kind of cold: How many times over the last 10 years have we had these moments where something breaks or something nearly breaks, where one person maintaining one tiny repro repository as a hobby or whatever happens to catch that something nefarious is going on and and saves us from the infrastructure of the internet completely crumbling? Now multiply that by a billion, when people have access to not only extremely advanced software in the form of these LLMs that everybody uses, but also the ability to task them to go out and do it themselves, with creating AI agents that are single-minded at accomplishing those things. We’re seeing a balance of two things happening this week. One is a bunch of the labs and companies like Google and OpenAI actually had people go out and find a bunch of vulnerabilities, including the one with PHP. And then we also have a bunch of people seeming to rush to take advantage of those vulnerabilities to try and hack into websites. So we have governments taking down websites, we have really popular websites that are going down briefly to be able to fix this vulnerability. This is a real reckoning moment, where we’re going to find out the downside risk of building so much of the internet on open source technology like PHP. When you really get down to the bone level of the internet, it is held together with glue and dreams. Anthony Ha: There’s so many things that were striking about this. One of them is the fact that — as I understand it, at least — this is not a new vulnerability. This is a vulnerability that has existed in PHP for decades. And PHP has been used as a programming language to build so much of the web, so this vulnerability has been there for decades, but no one knew about it. What happened is, essentially, that these big AI companies — including Wiz, now owned by Google — they were able to find these vulnerabilities using LLMs. [As noted above, I got this wrong: Human researchers participating in OpenAI and Wiz’s Hack the Planet initiative found the vulnerabilities , though they used AI to exploit the bug.] I guess part of the calculation is, we need to patch this, because if we can find this vulnerability using LLMs, so can other people. But the only way we can get the patch out there is to announce the vulnerability. And so it creates this very panicked situation where [they say]: “Okay, this vulnerability existed for decades. You have to patch right away, and if you can’t patch it right away, just take your website down. It’s that severe a vulnerability.”

articles.title: Block's new voice model sounds eerily human | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Block said that the voice model can run locally on a MacBook M4 Max
articles.body_text: Jack Dorsey’s Block released a new voice model out of the company’s research lab that runs locally and sounds strangely human with its expressions like laughs, pauses, and cries. The company said the model, called Dessa, is trained fully on human speech and a single NVIDIA GPU rack. Dessa is a full-duplex model, which means it can talk and listen at the same time, just like the GPT-Live model OpenAI released earlier this year . Typically, speech models are paired with a large language model for knowledge retrieval. Block said that Dessa’s knowledge stems from the conversational data it has. We believe voice is the most natural way to interact with intelligence, so we created Dessa, the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built. Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence. https://t.co/r0qFLdvd6c Block said that the current models can sound unnatural and annoying because they have text in the pipeline that drives speech generation. A lot of models like ElevenLabs v4 or Fish Audio Drama 3 use voice tags to drive emotion in speech generation. Dorsey’s company claims that emotion is built into its model. It’s not clear if that emotion is being steered by some kind of tags. “Interacting with current voice AI can just plain suck. It turns your voice into text and throws away an incredible amount of information text alone can’t carry. The most powerful AIs in the world can’t hear how you feel. We think that’s ridiculous, leads to a worse experience, and is potentially dangerous,” the company said in a blog post . The company’s researchers posted multiple examples of conversations with Dessa where the agent had different voices, cadences, and emotions. For instance, in the conversation, the bot said it was tired from work, and at that point it sounded tired. We made the first AI model you can have a realistic conversation with that was trained entirely on speech! Dessa is a full-duplex speech-to-speech model that you can run on consumer GPUs. This is a GPT3 moment for speech. pic.twitter.com/XVD8sSyJn8 In the example below, the bot was talking about the person making it comfortable while sounding emotional and almost breaking down. Dessa=full-duplex speech model vs Human=me, https://t.co/1eI6QFHo1w pic.twitter.com/zlZfxH2BA5 Another one shows a Block team member playing a game with the voice assistant. For the love of the game. Watch Cara play a guessing game with Dessa. The model guesses the first one right straight away, and the second doesn’t take long either. https://t.co/FDmoXNPpIh pic.twitter.com/I9f8saduEA The company said that the model can run locally on a consumer-grade computer such as a MacBook M4 Max or better. However, there is no public access to Dessa at the moment, and Block has put out a call for safety researchers to test the model. This is likely to test out cases where a voice agent could trick people on the other end.

articles.title: PHP-ocalypse: How two critical web bugs almost broke the internet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Two critical bugs in the PHP web programming language, used by the majority of the internet, threatened to upend the internet — and it's unlikely to be the last major software scare.
articles.body_text: On Wednesday, a decades-old open-source web technology called PHP almost broke the internet, thanks to two vulnerabilities that had sat dormant for years until researchers recently figured out a way to exploit them. The bugs are dubbed PHP2Shell , officially designated as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 . In simple terms, the bugs allow anyone who knows how to exploit them to break into an online system running PHP, such as a website or internet-facing server, without needing a password to access or modify its data. As situations go, this was a pretty sizable one, forcing millions of people around the world to scramble to patch their systems before malicious hackers could abuse them. The PHP Foundation, which maintains the PHP web software, publicly released patches on Wednesday that fixed the bugs, which when installed prevent web-facing servers from being attacked. The foundation had already given some of the biggest internet companies and web hosts that rely on PHP an early headstart on patching. Thanks to weeks of backroom chatter and careful coordination across the industry, the world — so far — broadly avoided mass internet exploitation. From Wednesday, governments began urging citizens and companies with websites to take action to mitigate the risks on their ends. A wide range of industries shuttered their websites and pulled services offline to patch their systems. Banks, retailers, gaming sites, online stores, hospitals, and some government agencies took down their servers to prevent attacks. But security researchers are warning that the situation isn’t over yet, and that a large number of systems around the world remain unpatched and vulnerable to hacks and data theft. This is also unlikely to be the last major internet software scare, with some expecting the advent of AI to rapidly uncover as-yet-undiscovered vulnerabilities that are waiting to be found and abused. Security researchers at Calif found two bugs in PHP, a programming language widely used around the world for building websites and web apps, both on the internet and hosted locally on company networks, like intranets and internal sites. PHP is open-source, meaning it’s free and available to be used by anyone for almost any reason. As such, it’s become one of the most popular and broadly used web programming languages on the web today. The two bugs were first discovered in 2024 but weren’t considered exploitable at the time, and weren’t patched. Security researchers recently found a way to exploit them, prompting them to alert the makers of the software to get them fixed. Calif alerted the PHP Foundation, which began a period of fixing the bugs and coordinated disclosure. The foundation did this by offering the information and patches about the security issues under a tightly guarded embargo — essentially held confidentially until a specific deadline — to give big companies an opportunity to get ahead of installing the fixes. PHP2Shell is pretty serious because it can be abused remotely over the internet and without the victim having to click on a link or open a file. This is known as remote code execution , and it’s one of the more damaging kinds of bugs to exploit because they can grant a hacker anywhere in the world effectively full control over an affected and unpatched system.

articles.title: Unprotected license plate surveillance cameras let anyone with a web browser tune in
articles.summary: The Verge is about technology and how it makes us feel. Founded in 2011, we offer our audience everything from breaking news to reviews to award-winning features and investigations, on our site, in video, and in podcasts.
articles.body_text: Automated license plate recognition systems, also known as ALPR or simply LPR systems, have become increasingly popular — and controversial — tools for law enforcement in recent years. The systems can automatically photograph and record data on license plates in real time, drawing the ire of privacy advocates like those at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, which has just released information on security vulnerabilities in ALPR systems across the country. “Earlier this year, EFF learned that more than a hundred ALPR cameras were exposed online, often with totally open Web pages accessible by anyone with a browser,” the organization says in the new report released today. The report focuses on systems sold by a company called PIPS Technology, which is now owned by 3M. According to the EFF, live feeds from some of the cameras were available to watch online, and “were individually connected to the internet and freely accessible online to anyone who knew where to look.” The organization described its testing approach: The testing process involved confirming that a camera was online and responding to requests by connecting to it with a Web browser or by connecting to it over Telnet. If the camera had a password on both the Web and Telnet interface we left it alone, but if the camera was not protected with a password we were able to recover configuration information. However, when the Web was locked down, but Telnet was not, we [were] able to view password information in the Telnet configuration. Often these passwords were set to the default or were otherwise not sophisticated enough to be secure.Using information embedded on the page and through publicly available sources, the EFF was able to identify the position of some of the cameras, and got in touch with the owners to highlight the vulnerabilities. Some, like local Louisiana law enforcement agencies and the University of Southern California, took steps to fix the vulnerabilities. But the city of Hialeah, Florida, stopped returning the organization’s calls. The ACLU has found that about three-quarters of law enforcement agencies were using similar systems in 2011, giving officers “hundreds of millions of data points” on drivers not accused of a crime.

Hertiginnan Meghans far Thomas Markle misstänks för barnpornografibrott och har anklagats för sexuella övergrepp på minderåriga. Redan 2019 slog Thomas Markles första fru Roslyn Loveless larm till brittisk polis. I ett sju sidor långt brev berättade hon om sina misstankar mot mannen hon var gift med 1964–1975. Enligt The Sun skrev hon om att hon ställt Thomas Markle mot väggen och frågat honom om han hade begått sexuella övergrepp mot barn. Han nekade, skriver exhustrun. ”Men han sa att han åkte till Filippinerna och Thailand eftersom 12-åringar är lagliga där.” Meghan, som är dotter till Thomas Markle och hans andra hustru Doria Ragland, informerades om misstankarna mot honom direkt, några månader efter att hon brutit med sin pappa i samband med bröllopet med prins Harry. Därefter har han vid flera tillfällen försökt reparera relationen till sin dotter. För knappt ett år sedan blev han svårt sjuk, fick en blodpropp och tvingades amputera benet på ett sjukhus i Filippinerna, dit han hade flyttat. Då gjorde han ett nytt försök – och fick ett brev till svar . Daily Mail var på plats när han öppnade brevet, men de fick aldrig veta vad Meghan skrivit. Nu skriver The Sun att det inte handlade om någon försoning. Tvärtom. I brevet skrev Meghan i stället att hon kände till att han ”utnyttjar unga flickor” och att myndigheterna också kände till det. Hon informerade honom även om att brevet var det sista han skulle höra av henne och att hon aldrig skulle låta honom träffa hennes barn.

articles.title: Möte med Netanyahu inför valet i Israel: ”Bibi”, vi älskar dig
articles.summary: Möte med Netanyahu inför valet i Israel: ”Bibi”, vi älskar dig
articles.body_text: Folkmassan jublar när Benjamin ”Bibi” Netanyahu kommer in på köpcentret i den israeliska valkampanjens slutspurt. De sjunger ”Bibi, kung av Israel” och ropar ”Vi älskar dig”. Här i den lilla staden Ramle verkar premiärministern gå mot en klar valseger ­– men mätningar pekar på ett mycket jämnt resultat. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Israels premiärminister Benjamin ”Bibi” Netanyahu håller valmöte i ett köpcenter i Ramle i Israel. Han hyllas av folkmassan som sjunger ”Bibi kung av Israel” – i staden som är ett högerfäste. Men mätningar pekar på fördel för mitten/vänsteroppositionen inför valet den 27 oktober. Israels premiärminister Benjamin Netanyahu slussas in i köpcentret i staden Ramle av ett väldigt säkerhetsuppbåd. Det är nästan fler säkerhetsmän och poliser på plats än människor som har kommit för att lyssna till sin älskade ”Bibi”, som han kallas av både vän och fiende. Här är Bibi, 77, verkligen älskad av folket. Här är han omgiven av ”bibister”, som hans mest övertygade anhängare kallas. Människor som är beredda att gå genom eld och vatten för ledaren – trots säkerhetsfiaskot den 7 oktober 2023 och alla andra kriser för Israel de senaste åren. – Jag älskar Bibi, det finns ingen som han. Han är född ledare, han har gjort saker som ingen annan klarat. Utan honom har vi inget land, mycket av hatet mot honom är avundsjuka, säger Zippi Cohen, 63, sjuksköterska i Ramle. – Jag är här för att stötta Bibi. Jag älskar honom, han är min ledare, han är stark i allt. Jag är förstagångsväljare men tvekar inte, andra kandidater snackar bara, säger Agam Chazan, 18, från Ramle som just gått ut gymnasiet och rycker in till värnplikten om en månad. Hon håller upp ett hemgjort plakat med texten ”Israels medborgare: Bibi” och en bild på premiärministern omgiven av en krona och ett hjärta.

articles.body_text: En tonårsflicka larmade om att hennes familjehemspappa utsatte henne för sexuella övergrepp – men trots det tvingades hon bo kvar. Familjehemspappan döms nu för sju fall av våldtäkt mot barn och ett sexuellt ofredande. Straffet blir fängelse i sex och ett halvt år. Det utsatta barnet är en flicka i tonåren som var familjehemsplacerad hemma hos mannen. – Det är försvårande att mannen utnyttjat flickans förtroende för honom, men det finns inte tillräckliga skäl att bedöma våldtäkterna som grova, säger Kajsa Malmström, rådman och rättens ordförande, i ett pressmeddelande. Flickan larmade själv Sundsvalls kommun, som var ansvariga för placeringen, och berättade att mannen utsatt henne för sexuella övergrepp. Trots det bestämde socialtjänsten att hon skulle bo kvar, enligt P4 Västernorrland . Det var först efter att flickan dokumenterat en av de misstänkta våldtäkterna som familjehemsplaceringen avbröts. Flickan flyttades då, mot sin vilja, till ett HVB -hem i en annan del av landet. Men vidhåll att alla har ett eget ansvar för sina handlingar. En självmordsnära person behöver träffa någon från psykiatrin på en gång. Ring 112 eller åk till en akutmottagning. Om möjligt – lämna inte personen ensam.

articles.title: Vatten överallt – SMHI varnar
articles.summary: Efter stormen Boelo varnar SMHI för högt vattenstånd längs hela Västkusten. I centrala Uddevalla syns nu stora översvämningar.
articles.body_text: Efter stormen Boelo varnar SMHI för högt vattenstånd längs hela Västkusten. I centrala Uddevalla syns nu stora översvämningar. Samtidigt skapar vädret problem på flera håll i Västsverige. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Efter nattens regnoväder är översvämmat på flera platser i centrala Uddevalla, rapporterar Bohusläningen . Enligt tidningen så ”sprutar vatten ur brunnarna” vid Kampenhof resecentrum och det är även svårt att ta sig fram med bil på bland annat Bastiongatan. Bilder från Uddevalla visar stora vattenmängder på parkeringar och vägar, och fordon som försöker ta sig fram genom översvämningarna. Även längre ner mot Västkusten är det problem med översvämmade vägar och tåg har ställts in på grund av ovädret. I Göteborg föll ett träd över en kontaktledning vid Linnéplatsen, vilket orsakade stopp för spårvagnarna, rapporterar GP . Samtidigt blockerades ett körfält på Ringön efter översvämningar, rapporterar tidningen. SMHI har utfärdat en gul varning för högt vattenstånd längs hela Västkusten. Vattenståndet väntas stiga till upp mot en meter under natten mot måndagen. Kring Orust och Tjörn kan nivåerna lokalt nå 120 centimeter. Höga vågor väntas samtidigt längs Bohuskusten. För Hallandskusten och stora delar av Bohuskusten gäller även en gul vindvarning. Under måndagen väntas mycket hårda västliga eller sydvästliga vindbyar, och närmast kusten kan stormbyar nå 21–25 meter per sekund. Blåsten kan orsaka förseningar i kollektivtrafiken och leda till nedfallna träd. SMHI uppmanar också till att förankra lösa föremål som studsmattor och utemöbler.
